You are correct: there is a great appeal about additions and changes to Minecraft. But, that's not exclusive to Minecraft updates; the core definition of a mod is just that: additions, changes, and, sometimes, deletions. That's the reason why the modding community is huge now and it's to be expected of many games and not just Minecraft.

The problem with the continual updates to Minecraft, though, is the fact that they are updates. On a private server I play on, we went through several map changes throughout the years from the constant updates and, though I still play indefinitely, it scared off a lot of the best players on the server.

People like myself were beginning to grow tired of the updates because most of the things they added could've easily been added by mods. I'm sure that a lot of the infrastructure behind the scenes has been improved greatly over time, but it's not worth the constant changes. I wanted a game that can be considered 'finished' and not have to worry about whether or not what I build on that server will have to be scrapped in favor of the new map from the updates.

I got frustrated and locked my Minecraft single player version at 1.6.4 with some mods and proclaimed that I'm not going to update until Minecraft is finally finished, whether that day comes or not.

Even though my frustrations should've ended right there, a big aspect of Minecraft is the multiplayer. The fact that servers have more incentive to update since most players like to have an up-to-date Minecraft made me grow angrier at the Minecraft devs for not finishing the game yet.

So, in conclusion, here are the pros and cons I feel about Minecraft updates:

Pros

  • More features, blocks, and items.

Cons

  • Most of the features that the updates add could be added by mods.

  • Breaks maps every few months.

  • The game can be changed in a way that some people don't like; updates are not optional, mods are.

  • Frustrates me.

Overall, my view is that Minecraft would be better off focusing on a straightforward modding API and finishing the game. It would solve a lot of problems.

Death in the Forest

As a successor to the private mod pack FamishedForest 2, FamishedForest 3 brings the challenge of hardcore survival in the woods to the public. The mod pack is focused on the 'progression' mechanic that has generally been ignored in most other mod packs.

Development started on 28 May 2014, anticipated for my FamishedForest 3 YouTube 'Let's Play'.

Download (MC v1.6.4)

FamishedForest-3.0.7z (44 MiB)

How to Install

Click here to see a tutorial video.

  1. Download the mod pack.

  2. Open the archive with a file archiver.

  3. Extract the contents (not the folder) of the MinecraftDirectory folder to where your game is installed. Typically, it's the .minecraft folder for Windows and Linux, or minecraft for Mac.

  4. Copy the FamishedForest-3 folder (the folder itself) to a permanent place on your computer — probably in the same place you have your minecraft folder. We'll reference this folder later.

  5. Launch Minecraft. Select New Profile. Name the profile "FamishedForest 3" or something. Make sure your Game Directory points to your FamishedForest-3 folder you copied earlier. Under Use version:, select "release 1.6.4-Forge9.11.1.965" from the drop-down. Finally, make sure JVM Arguments: checkbox is selected and type "-Xmx3G" in the box next to it.

  6. Click Save Profile. Select your newly-created profile from the drop-down list and you're good to go!
